findings.evidence: roadmap README lines 295-303: first bullet enumerates the three prerequisites and ends "these give `A ⊗_K Aᵒᵖ` Brauer-trivial"; second bullet ends "Each Brauer class has a **unique division-algebra representative** (Layer 2 uniqueness)." `grep -n "Layer 6" TauCeti/Algebra/BrauerGroup/*.lean` shows `Trivial.lean:98` already claiming the first bullet and `Group.lean:89` the second.
findings.fix: Cite the Layer 6 second bullet's "unique division-algebra representative (Layer 2 uniqueness)" clause (the base case of it) together with the Layer 2 uniqueness this consumes and the Hamilton worked-example clause, rather than the first bullet; update the PR description to match.
findings.issue: The References section claims this "completes the first bullet of Layer 6 (\"the API that the identity and inverse rest on\")", but that bullet lists only `End_K V` Brauer-equivalent to `K`, `Mₙ(K)` Brauer-trivial, and matrix absorption -- all already implemented, as `Trivial.lean:98` itself states ("This implements the Brauer-triviality prerequisites of the first bullet of Layer 6"). The result proved here is the base case of the Layer 6 *second* bullet's clause "Each Brauer class has a unique division-algebra representative (Layer 2 uniqueness)", which is also what the old `Trivial.lean` docstring pointed at ("which the roadmap places with the Wedderburn invariants"). The PR description repeats the same wrong bullet.

summary: Formal and informal sources are credited (Gille-Szamuely, Pierce, the roadmap, the in-repo Wedderburn-uniqueness engine), and nothing is vendored or laundered. The one defect is that the roadmap target named in the References section and the PR description is the wrong bullet.
